A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 18-page versions of Lens. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are accessible and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v4 reports original classification, traffic-generation, tokenization and ablation results in Tables 2 and 4-11 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 reports original classification, new-class adaptation, traffic-generation, synthetic-data utility and ablation results in the main text and Appendices B-C.

M1.justification: On the retained T5 backbone, v5 replaces hexadecimal WordPiece inputs and the MSP/POP/HTP objective with parsed textual traffic, BBPE tokenization, knowledge-guided masking and auxiliary context pretraining. It adds explicit label options, prefix-trie constrained decoding and adaptation using new-class data to v4's existing generative classification procedure.

E1.justification: The six traffic datasets and five header-generation targets remain. However, v5 removes binary Tor, malware and DoH detection, revises several class inventories, and adds scenarios involving 1, 3 or 5 new classes and training detectors on synthetic traffic. It also reports mini-C4 use for tokenizer training.

E2.justification: v5 adds TrafficLLM to the reported classification and generation comparisons, expanding generation beyond v4's sole NetShare comparator. ET-BERT-LwF is additionally evaluated in the new-class experiments. The seven existing classification baseline methods remain represented.

E3.justification: v5 specifies 60% stratified pretraining samples instead of v4's remaining-data approach. Classification flow inputs change from three to 34 packets, and generation uses one sampled packet per flow. Main-text budgets change from 56,000 pretraining steps and 10 fine-tuning epochs to 130,000 and 20. New-class and synthetic-to-real testing protocols are added, while the IP Diversity Ratio metric is removed.

E4.justification: v4's tokenizer comparison, loss-weight search and MSP/POP/HTP/no-pretraining ablations are replaced by KG-MSP/context ablations, random-masking comparisons and masking-probability sensitivity tests. v5 also adds analyses of head versus rare attack classes and per-class outcomes during classification extension (Table 4 and Appendices B-C).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The additional sensitivity tables and per-class sample counts in v5 do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Classification, generation and ablation results are extensively replaced. For example, v4 Table 5 reports average accuracy of 0.9663 for flows and 0.9784 for packets across 15 tasks; v5 Table 3 reports 0.9633 across 12 tasks. These changed conditions preclude interpreting the difference as a performance regression. New extension and detector-utility results are added, and IP-diversity results disappear.

T1.justification: v4's formal POP and HTP losses, weighted joint objective (Equations 2-4), and IP Diversity Ratio definition are removed. v5 Equation 1 retains the existing autoregressive negative-log-likelihood form with different masking. Changes are limited to these definitions; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace v4's first-T5, tokenizer-selection, three-objective and 50-95% label-saving contribution framing with knowledge-guided pretraining, context-based extension to new classes and synthetic-traffic utility. Supporting both classification and generation remains the overarching goal.

C2.justification: v5 replaces explanations centered on packet/flow granularity and the three pretraining objectives with interpretations involving network-field semantics, textual context and label-distribution shifts. It discusses TrafficLLM's advantages on some generated fields, explicitly limits the extension study to demonstrating extensibility rather than proposing continual learning, and explains the header-generation boundary and payload replay/encryption options.

D1.justification: Appendices A, D and E add preprocessing tools, 12-byte payload extraction, packet-length statistics, input examples and detailed architecture/optimizer settings. v5 also documents TurboT5 and four A6000 GPUs, while replacing v4's exact fine-tuning flow/packet counts with percentage-based disclosures. Its code statement is a future publication-contingent release promise.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around works including netFound, NetMamba, TrafficLLM, TrafficGPT and NetDiffusion. The central distinction shifts from combining encoder-decoder capabilities and custom pretraining tasks to network-knowledge integration and extensible classification. Table 1 accordingly replaces the custom-pretraining criterion with knowledge-guided pretraining.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around knowledge guidance and extensibility. Experimental subsections are reorganized, and the former generation-centered appendix becomes Appendices A-E covering data, analyses, input examples and hyperparameters. The title and author presentation also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2 are substantially redrawn. v4's seven distribution figures are removed, while v5 adds the detector-performance chart and model-input examples. Classification tables are reshaped, and the previously separate main-text and appendix generation tables are consolidated into v5 Table 6. Numerous new analysis and documentation tables alter the layout.

improvement.justification: v5 strengthens validation through TrafficLLM generation comparisons, synthetic-to-real detector evaluation and targeted masking/context controls, addressing v4's reliance on NetShare and distribution metrics for generation. These provide a modest net quality gain. Reproducibility remains limited by differing descriptions of the random-masking control in Section 3.2.1 and Appendix B.1, and unreconciled fine-tuning durations of 20 epochs versus a maximum of 40 in Table 17. The extension evidence also requires qualification: Lens improves accuracy over ET-BERT-LwF but has lower F1 in five of six settings.
